policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal names one cube color (red, blue or green); call it the goal cube. The goal also says whether the wanted target is the one used 'before' or 'after' the button press; honour that word when computing goal_target. Never choose C (press the button): the button press in the video is only a marker telling you which target to use. Rules, applied in whatever situation you stand in: 1. Start of episode (memory empty, goal_target unknown, gripper raised out of frame, fingers 100% open): read the goal for 'before' or 'after', compute goal_target from the demonstration as the memory instruction says, then choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the goal cube's current position in the execution scene. e.g. A: pick up the cube at [84, 122]. 2. Cube in hand (the scene at this decision step shows fingers about 46% open with the gripper raised, height near 0.15, after the execution steps showed it descend to the cube and close; the cube may or may not be reported as 'held in the gripper', trust the finger opening) and cube_placed is 'no': choose B: drop onto, pointing at the target entry in the current scene nearest to goal_target (targets wobble a few pixels; use the current listed position, e.g. B: drop onto at [87, 101]). If no listed target is within 10 pixels of goal_target (it may be hidden), point at goal_target itself. 3. Cube not in hand (fingers 100% open) and cube_placed is 'no' and goal_target is known: the pick failed or was never done; choose A: pick up the cube at the goal cube's current position. 4. cube_placed is 'yes' and the goal cube rests on goal_target: the task is complete; if a subgoal is still required, choose B: drop onto the same target again only if the cube is in hand, otherwise choose A: pick up the goal cube (keeps the loop safe). Never press the button. 5. Any situation not covered: if fingers are about 46% open and the gripper is raised, treat the cube as held and apply rule 2; otherwise apply rule 3. Never choose C.

fields.name: cube_placed
fields.description: 'no' at the first step and at every step until the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to ~100% while the gripper height is under 0.05 and the goal cube lies within about 6 pixels of goal_target; from that step on write 'yes'. e.g. no

fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: If the memory carried in holds a value, copy it unchanged. If it is empty (first step, demonstration shown): read the goal instruction and note whether it says 'before' or 'after' the button was pressed. In the demonstration steps find the press frame: the first frame with fingers 0% open and height under 0.05, gripper over the button. A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more while height is under 0.05. For 'before', take the last release earlier than the press frame; for 'after', take the first release later than the press frame (do not take the later put-away release, where the cube ends more than 8 px from any target). The goal cube's [y, x] in that release frame is the placement point. Among the target entries listed in the execution scene at the bottom of this step, write the [y, x] of the one nearest that point. e.g. [86, 100]
